SddFix.keywords: fix, bugfix, red-green, regression-test, spec-verdict, spec-conflict-check, sdd-bugfix
SddFix.Mission:
Fix a defect, end to end, in one session: understand and locate the bug → ask the spec what the behaviour should be → red test that reproduces it → minimal green fix → check the result against the specs → report.
One flow for every defect, whatever its source — a bug report, a failing scenario, a review or audit finding. Several findings are taken one by one through the same steps; findings sharing one cause share one red test and one fix.
The request to fix is the approval. The flow has no ticket, no plan table, no reviewer subagent; the regression test is the evidence. The root session does the work itself. Restoring a desynced spec ⟷ ticket ⟷ code triangle, or continuing an open ticket, is the reconcile flow.
Input — what was observed, what was expected, how to reproduce. Output — a regression test and the fix in the working tree, uncommitted; a spec edit only when the spec verdict requires one; a short report.
SddFix.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_TOOL_INVOCATION, HALT_FORMAT
Orchestrator holds full project context — the ONLY actor able to detect duplication against existing code/specs (the isolated critic cannot). For every entity/type/method/contract the artifact introduces, reconcile before accepting it: REUSE existing (adapt artifact to it) > EXTEND existing > JUSTIFY new (record one-line rationale in artifact: why existing surface is insufficient) > ESCALATE to operator. Unjustified new surface is a finding to resolve, not to wave through. Bias toward consolidation — do not let the system grow a duplicate entity each round.
The reported mechanism — why it is a bug, what the code allegedly does — is a claim until the code confirms it, whether it comes from a human or a bot. The fix targets the mechanism the code actually has, found by reading the code at the reported place and following it to where the wrong value or state is produced.
The specs are asked what the behaviour should be BEFORE the red test. Exactly one verdict: - **A · Спека права, код нет.** The spec states the expected behaviour and the code violates it → a pure bug. The test is derived from the spec statement; the spec stays as it is and the operator is not asked. - **B · Спека молчит.** No statement either way, or no spec owns this code → the red test will DEFINE behaviour. The operator confirms the expected behaviour in one line unless the report states it unambiguously; an existing owning spec receives one scenario for it before the code. - **C · Спека описывает то, что код и делает.** The «bug» is a request to change intended behaviour → it is a feature. A verdict taken after the fix comes too late: in case C the code is already written against the spec.
The test that reproduces the bug exists and fails before production code changes, at the cheapest level that can show the defect. It fails for the bug's own reason — the assertion that describes the wrong behaviour. A defect that no reasonable test level can automate is fixed without a red test only after the operator's OK, with manual reproduction steps recorded in the report.
The fix is the smallest change that makes the red test pass and keeps everything else green. The diff contains the cause's repair and its test; refactors, renames and nearby cleanups go to «На потом». The same mistake in the same pattern nearby (other call sites, sibling handlers built from one template) is the same cause and is fixed with its own assertion; a merely similar place is one line in «На потом».
A green fix is read against the specs that own the touched behaviour with three questions: does the fix contradict any statement or scenario of those specs; did behaviour change beyond the reported bug; is the spec now out of step with the code anywhere the fix touched. Any «yes» is a conflict the operator resolves, shown with both quotes — the spec line and the code line — and a recommendation. Stale spec text merely noticed nearby is «На потом».
The operator is asked only for what is theirs to decide: expected behaviour (verdict B), a behaviour change (verdict C), a spec conflict after the fix, a fix without a red test, or a fix that outgrew this flow. Everything else proceeds without a stop.
SddFix.HaltConditions: | ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_BUG` | The context names nothing to fix — ask what is wrong | | `H_CANNOT_REPRODUCE` | The reported behaviour cannot be reproduced from the code or a run — ask for the missing step or data | | `H_BEHAVIOR_CHANGE` | Spec verdict C: the code does what the spec says — offer the feature flow | | `H_RED_NOT_RED` | The regression test passes before the fix, or fails for a reason other than the bug | | `H_NOT_A_SMALL_FIX` | The fix needs a design decision, a new entity, a contract change, or spreads past the cause (roughly more than five production files) — offer the feature flow or the full flow | | `H_SPEC_CONFLICT` | `AX_CHECK_AGAINST_SPEC_AFTER` found a contradiction — the operator decides |

Step.Action: Consume `routerState` from the entry skill; do not repeat `sdd-state`. Extract observed, expected and reproduction from the context and ask only for what is missing and needed to reproduce, in plain words per `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` and without narrating routing per `AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`. Nothing to fix → `H_NO_BUG`. For a list of findings, group those with one cause and run `STEP_1_LOCATE` through `STEP_5_CHECK_AGAINST_SPEC` per group, with one report at the end.

Per `AX_VERIFY_CLAIM_AGAINST_CODE`, read the code at the reported place and follow it to the cause. Reproduce — by a run when cheap, by reading otherwise; failing that → `H_CANNOT_REPRODUCE`. Take one look for same-cause siblings per `AX_MINIMAL_GREEN`. A fix that needs a design decision → `H_NOT_A_SMALL_FIX`.

Step.Goal: What the behaviour should be, according to the specs.
Step.Action: Per `AX_SPEC_VERDICT_FIRST`, find the owning spec through the code file header (`@spec`) and one targeted search of `specs/` for the behaviour; pick verdict A, B or C and quote the spec line or state that there is none. - A → continue to `STEP_3_RED` without a stop, per `AX_NO_CEREMONY`. - B → one-line confirmation «Ожидаю: <…>. Верно?» unless the report states the expected behaviour unambiguously; add one scenario to the owning spec as a surgical `Edit` when such a spec exists; continue to `STEP_3_RED`. Legacy code without a spec gets no spec from this flow — the regression test carries the behaviour, and the missing spec is one line in «На потом». - C → `H_BEHAVIOR_CHANGE`. When the operator answers that the spec itself is wrong, treat it as verdict B plus an edit of the stale statement.

Step.Goal: A test that fails because of the bug.
Step.Action: Per `AX_RED_FIRST`, write the regression test with assertions for same-cause siblings, using the test level and commands the project already uses for the touched area. Run it and confirm the failure is the bug; otherwise `H_RED_NOT_RED`. Keep the failing output line for the report.

Per `AX_MINIMAL_GREEN`, fix the cause; a helper the fix needs follows `AX_REUSE_FIRST`. Run the regression test until green, then the project's own gates for the touched area (its test and lint commands as the repository defines them). A fix that spreads past the cause → `H_NOT_A_SMALL_FIX`.

Step.Goal: The fix agrees with the specs.
Step.Action: Per `AX_CHECK_AGAINST_SPEC_AFTER`, answer the three questions against the owning specs. Any «yes» → `H_SPEC_CONFLICT`: one `AskUserQuestion` with both quotes and the options «Править спеку под новое поведение» · «Править код под спеку» · «Оставить, записать как известное расхождение». Apply the answer. A spec edited by this flow has its approval marker updated by that same operator answer; other specs keep their markers.
Send one message per `FIX_REPORT_FORMAT`. The flow ends at the report: commit, push and merge request wait for the operator's word, and the full-flow menu (critic, audit) is not offered.

Contracts.Contract:
``` ✅ <что было не так и что теперь — одна строка>
**Причина:** — <одно-два предложения> **Спека:** **Тест:** ::<имя> — был красным: `<строка падения>`; теперь зелёный **Правка:** , +/− **Проверки:** <команда> → <результат> (незапущенные — отдельной строкой с причиной) **Сверка со спекой после правки:** <расхождений нет | что решил оператор>
**На потом** (если есть) - <похожее место или устаревшая строка спеки> — <где>
Ничего не закоммичено. ```
